messages:
alex: heads-up — i'm seeing host-pinned buffer fragmentation on the nvlink boxes when we keep long-lived staging buffers for async offload. performance slowly degrades after ~12 hours.

maria: hmm, is this the cudaHostAlloc path or our fallback mmap pinned allocator?

alex: cudaHostAlloc. pattern: allocate 2x staging buffers per model shard, keep them pinned for the lifetime of a session to avoid repeated mapping churn.

sam: that was the thing we optimized to reduce mapping syscalls, right? surprised about fragmentation — pinned should be contiguous-ish.

alex: it's more about address space and page-table fragmentation. small frees between large allocations leave holes, cuda's driver doesn't compact. on machines with lots of short-lived infer jobs we end up with OOMs even though total free pages > needed for a new big contiguous allocation.

jin: can we use cudaHostRegister on large malloc'd regions and sub-alloc? i remember that can avoid repeated kernel APIs but still give us control to defrag within our arena.

maria: tradeoff: cudaHostRegister requires the memory be resident in user space and pinned at register time, plus it's slower for the initial pin. but it lets us manage a large slab and do suballoc.

sam: idea: keep a single large host-slabs-per-gpu and implement a suballocator with best-fit + periodic coalescing. then only call cudaHostRegister on the whole slab.

alex: that could work. questions: 1) fallback for customers who want strict per-session isolation 2) QoS when multiple processes share host memory (containers) 3) how to evict long-lived pinned pages if we need memory for a higher-priority request.

maria: (1) we can expose a config: session.isolated_pinned = true/false. default false for perf. isolated true will do per-session pinned allocs (current behavior).

jin: (2) for containers we need namespacing; a slab per cgroup or per-tenant may suffice. otherwise kernel pinning across processes is messy.

sam: (3) eviction: pinned pages can't be swapped. but we could implement a priority queue + graceful fallback: if new request needs more contiguous pinned region, attempt to migrate less-recently-used pinned buffers back to device memory or copy to pageable and unpin. that's heavy but doable.

alex: related: we should add metrics so we can observe host-pinned fragmentation: e.g., total pinned bytes, largest-contiguous-chunk, pinned-alloc-failures, avg-allocation-latency.

jin: + trace spans on host alloc/free with stack tags so we can correlate to model lifecycle.

maria: implementation proposal: 1) add HostSlabManager which reserves a large virtual region via malloc+madvise(hugepages?) 2) call cudaHostRegister once per slab 3) suballoc with a small internal free-list + opportunistic coalesce 4) expose policy: slab-per-gpu, slab-per-tenant, slab-per-process.

sam: sound plan. edge-case: what about pinned memory used for direct RDMA / nvlink DMA? driver requirements might want page-aligned or certain flags. need to validate that cudaHostRegister slab works for peer copies.

alex: good call. i'll run a quick check against nvlink copy apis.

infra-bot: snapshot: created perf/issue 2897 for host-pinned fragmentation investigations (priority: P2).

maria: for the RFC follow-up we should include microbenchmarks: alloc/free churn, largest-chunk over time, worst-case time-to-allocate for big shard loads. also show fallback copy latency when we have to migrate pinned -> device -> pinned.

jin: + add a small sim in python that models fragmentation given our allocation/free traces (we can reuse traces from the perf lab). helps pick slab sizes and coalescing thresholds.

sam: question about config surface: should we auto-tune slab size per-host based on physical RAM and expected concurrency? or keep user-configured?

alex: auto-tune with safe caps seems best. defaults: slab = min(16GB, 0.2 * host_ram) for inference nodes, with opt-out. we'll record heuristics in the RFC.

maria: next steps: alex to draft RFC + perf sim, jin to validate cudaHostRegister/nvlink compat, sam to sketch metrics/tracing schema. i'll own driving the doc and validation checklist.

alex: thanks — i'll start the RFC today and drop a link here when it's up. :thumbsup:
